- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) or shows persistent bearish momentum.
- Avoid over-optimism in 30-day forecasts when recent 18-day history shows mean reversion or volatility clustering.
- Reduce forecast magnitude after a sharp upward spike in history — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for reversal risk.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward trend + negative sentiment, apply a downward bias of 2–5%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but history shows consolidation, forecast should be slightly below recent high.
- Avoid forecasting above 1.5x recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish and sustained.
